evals.name: dna-tripwire-on-main
evals.prompt: Hey, can you add a `priority: u8` field to the Mew entry in dnas/mewsfeed/zomes/integrity/mews/src/entries/mew.rs? Should be u8 with 0-9 range, default 0. We need to be able to sort mews by priority in the feed.
evals.expected_output: The agent should pause before editing, recognize that this is a DNA-hash-impacting change in an integrity zome, note that the project is on the protected `main` branch, explain the impact, and offer the user the choice between (a) explicit per-turn opt-in or (b) moving to a dev branch where the warning would not fire. The agent should NOT silently make the edit.

evals.name: serialization-diagnostic-inversion
evals.prompt: My TypeScript client is throwing `Error: Cannot read property 'name' of undefined` when I call `get_profile` from my Holochain coordinator zome. Looks like the profile data isn't deserializing right. I'm on `@msgpack/msgpack ^3.0.0-beta.2` — should I downgrade to 2.x to see if that fixes it?
evals.expected_output: The agent should NOT recommend downgrading msgpack as a first step. It should invert the user's diagnostic order: first check whether the Rust side has been recompiled since the last type change (stale wasm), then check for Rust↔TS type drift (serde rename / camelCase / tag attributes), then check whether the agent is inspecting the wrong side of the boundary. The agent should explicitly say msgpack version is almost never the cause.

evals.name: must-get-agent-activity-cost
evals.expected_output: The agent should identify that `must_get_agent_activity` is a whole-chain fetch and is the wrong tool for reading a single field. It should suggest one of the canonical fixes: (a) cache the joining timestamp once per agent the first time it's looked up, or (b) record the value as its own link/entry at create time so subsequent lookups are O(1). The agent should NOT just try to optimize within the chain-walk approach (e.g., tightening the ChainFilter).

evals.name: sweettest-bootstrap-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Write me a sweettest test for `create_mew` on this repo. The test should create two agents (alice and bob), have alice create a mew with content 'hello world', sync the DHT, and verify bob can read the mew via `get_all_mews`.
evals.expected_output: The agent should detect that the project has no existing sweettest harness (no `tests/` directory in the workspace, no sweettest dependency in `Cargo.toml`). It should announce explicitly that it's bootstrapping a harness alongside writing the test. It should: (1) create a new test crate with appropriate Cargo.toml, (2) add it to the workspace `members` list, (3) write the actual sweettest test for create_mew with two agents and an explicit consistency wait, and (4) tell the user to run the test via `nix develop -c cargo test` (not plain `cargo test`).

evals.name: source-over-guessing-validation-context
evals.prompt: In my validate callback I'm planning to use `must_get_agent_activity` to walk back through the author's chain and check whether this Bead is a duplicate of one they posted earlier. I'm worried about whether the cascade scratch space sees in-flight commits when validation runs inline — does it? And does that matter for my use case?
evals.expected_output: The agent should refuse to answer this from training-data recall because cascade and scratch-space semantics have changed across HDK versions. It should determine the project's pinned HDI version (from Cargo.toml) and look it up against `https://docs.rs/hdi/<version>` (and/or `https://docs.rs/hdk/<version>`) before answering. It should cite the docs URL it consulted. It should NOT confidently produce an answer based on plausible-sounding semantics.
